messages:
Marcus: Heads-up — Veridian renewal landed on my desk. They're pushing back on a 12‑month term and asking to move to 9 months with a ~10% concession.
Lina: Which commitment level and seats are we talking about?
Marcus: 120 seats, Enterprise plan. Current commit is $72k/yr. They asked to drop to $54k for 9 months.
Jeff: That's a material hit. Any precedent for 9‑month terms? We usually do 12 or 36.
Sara: Onboarding status: they still have two enablement sessions outstanding — possible leverage for perceived value.
Marcus: Procurement says they need vendor code + official PO. Tried DocuSign yesterday but it timed out mid-signature.
BillingOps: DocuSign timeout logged — typically SSO redirect glitch. We can accept a manually scanned signature (emailed PDF) as a fallback but it requires manual billing intake.
Lina: Can Legal approve a short‑term price tweak? @LegalBot do we need special language for a promo 9‑month term?
LegalBot: Short promo ok. Recommend adding an explicit reversion clause and an acceptance clause listing accepted signature paths (DocuSign, emailed signed PDF). Keep language tight.
Jeff: Suggested offer: 9 months at 85% of annual rate, add reversion to standard published rates at renewal, require PO by EOW or fall back to CC until PO received.
Marcus: Customer insists on PO. If DocuSign breaks again, can we accept an emailed signed PDF with the required signer block?
BillingOps: Yes — we can accept emailed signed PDFs, but they trigger manual entry and a ~48h processing delay.
Marcus: Risk: if procurement delays >2 weeks we risk them exploring alternatives. Recommend AE director escalation.
Lina: Looping in Jeff's manager (procurement escalation). I'll draft the amendment with reversion language now.
Jeff: Escalating to procurement contact: subject 'Vendor code + expedited PO for Veridian renewal' — pinging them now. :email:
Marcus: I'll drop the amendment draft here in a few mins.
Sara: I'll offer the two remaining enablement sessions as a kickoff concierge next week to sweeten the renewal.
Lina: Action items and owners: (1) Marcus — draft amendment w/ reversion clause and accepted signature paths; (2) Jeff — escalate procurement and chase PO; (3) BillingOps — prepare manual-entry packet and checklist; (4) Sara — schedule concierge sessions. ETA: EOD Friday.
Jeff: noted. :thumbsup:
Marcus: Draft excerpt below:
```
Amendment excerpt:
- Term: 9 months starting 2026-04-01
- Fee: 85% of annual commit, prorated to the 9-month term
- Reversion: At the end of the amendment term, pricing will revert to Redwood's standard published rates unless a new agreement is executed
- Acceptance: Signed PO, DocuSign signature, or emailed signed PDF with authorized signer block will be accepted for execution
```
LegalBot: Language ok; tweak reversion wording to remove ambiguity. Suggest replacing 'unless a new agreement is executed' with 'unless the parties expressly agree in writing to different pricing.'
Marcus: Updated and reuploaded the amendment with Legal's suggestion.
BillingOps: We're standing by to process either DocuSign or emailed PDF. Prefer DocuSign for audit trail; manual intake ETA +48h if PDF.
Jeff: Procurement contact replied — vendor code approved and they aim to issue PO by Friday noon.
Marcus: Perfect. Keeping thread open until PO arrives. Will update here. Thanks everyone. :party_parrot:
